title: tapBoth runs exactly one of its two handlers and does not replace the Result it observes
notes: The deliberate pair of 01-result-lifting/result-tap-and-tap-error-observe-without-changing, which pins the one-sided observers. `tap` fires only on success and `tapError` only on failure, so neither case can see an observer that runs on BOTH variants; `tapBoth` is the member where running exactly one handler is the whole contract, and the order of the first two lines is what says so — one `tapBoth` call pushed `ok …` and the other pushed `error …`, so neither call ran both handlers and neither ran the wrong one. The last two lines prove the observed Result was passed through unchanged, exactly as the tap/tapError case proves it: `Ada Lovelace` survives to `unwrapOr` on the success path and `none` on the failure path, so the observation replaced neither variant. Like `flatten`, `tapBoth` was implemented and tested on the runtime (poc/src/runtime/result.ts) while no `.sm` program could call it, and the refusal was SMITHERS1301 — an unrecognized member leaves the Result unconsumed — rather than an unknown-property error, so nothing went red while the member sat unreachable. THE `xfail(go)` MARKER WAS RETIRED 2026-08-28 together with the `flatten` one, by the same two coordinated edits to `compiler/forkbridge/lowering.go.txt`: `tapBoth` is now in `resultConsumerMembers` and declared on both `SmithersOk` and `SmithersErr`. The closing note the marker left behind was honoured rather than skipped — both fork declarations validate the handler object before choosing a branch, so a missing handler panics with the reference's own message instead of being silently not observed, and the panic fires on BOTH variants rather than only on the one whose handler is absent. (The fork's `match` still does NOT validate its handler object, which the reference does; that is a separate, still-open divergence no corpus case probes.) `compiler/fork_result_member_surface_test.go` now fails if the fork's member list and the reference's `RESULT_MEMBER_SIGNATURES` drift apart again. The obligation this case discharges: specification/failures.mdx, "Matching and Transformation", lists the required observation members as `tap tapAsync tapError tapErrorAsync tapBoth tapBothAsync` under the heading "Observation, which MUST NOT change the Result", and both halves of that sentence are pinned here — `tapBoth` exists, and it does not change the Result.
